subject: Data Processing Addendum — KMS requirement & signature timeline
messages:
From: Ellen Price <ellen.price@brighthealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: t.liu@brighthealth.com, procurement@brighthealth.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data Processing Addendum — Clarification on KMS & EU transfers

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Procurement and Legal at BrightHealth reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and came back with two gating items before procurement can accept:

1) Customer-managed keys / BYOK: our security policy requires a customer-controlled KMS option (BYOK or HSM) for certain PHI-derived datasets.
2) EU-to-US transfers: we need explicit wording and an accompanying Data Transfer Addendum that covers SCCs or an equivalent mechanism.

We attached our redlines for the DPA (BrightHealth_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf) and a short KMS requirements doc. Our procurement team is on a hard deadline and prefers execution via DocuSign. Can Redwood confirm whether you can support BYOK or provide a clear technical design and timeline for a KMS solution?

Thomas (cc) will coordinate the procurement side. We'd like to get to signature by COB 2026-12-06 if possible. If Redwood cannot support BYOK, please propose acceptable mitigations (EU-only residency, in-region private deployment, or contractual limits on PHI processing).

Thanks,
Ellen Price
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
BrightHealth

[Attachment: BrightHealth_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: KMS_requirements_summary.docx (docx)]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Ellen Price <ellen.price@brighthealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data Processing Addendum — Clarification on KMS & EU transfers

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear note and for sending the redlines. I’ve looped in Rishi (Legal) and Karthik (Account Lead).

Short answers up front:
- We currently do not support customer-hosted KMS/BYOK in the hosted product out of the box.
- We can offer Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed network and some key management integrations, and for enterprise deals we have patterns for HSM-backed keys with our cloud partners.

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi to review your redlines and propose contractual language that protects BrightHealth while keeping our standard controls.
2) If BYOK is a hard requirement, we’ll prepare a risk/exception request for leadership and security to review with a proposed technical approach.
3) We can also present a fallback: Dedicated EU-only deployment to keep data resident in-region while longer-term KMS work is scoped.

We understand the 12/06 timeline — we’ll try to accelerate where possible and flag blockers.

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

[Referenced: BrightHealth_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood DPA redlines & KMS note

Vanessa / Karthik —

I reviewed BrightHealth's redlines and prepared our counter-redlined DPA (Redwood_DPA_standard_v3_redlined.pdf). High-level thoughts:

- Subprocessors: we can add a commitment to provide 30 days' notice of new subprocessors and offer a short stop-gap right to object for critical data types. We can’t accept unlimited veto rights.
- Data transfers: we'll offer SCCs plus an explicit reference to our EU data residency options; we cannot sign a perpetual obligation beyond industry norms but will include a mapping to our transfer safeguards.
- KMS/BYOK: legal & security will not agree to a contractual statement that we support fully customer-controlled BYOK for the hosted service without a technical design and an attestation from infra. If BrightHealth requires BYOK for PHI-derived datasets, we need to evaluate: (a) whether Dedicated/Private deployment can meet their requirement; or (b) if BYOK in hosted is feasible, it will be an engineering project with a multi-week timeline and program-level security review.

I attached our redlines and a suggested exception request template. If the customer insists on execution by 12/06, we should determine whether a time-limited conditional acceptance (e.g., sign pending a formal technical assessment and a mutually-agreed Statement of Work) is acceptable.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_standard_v3_redlined.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: Exception_Request_Template.pdf (pdf)]

From: Thomas Liu <t.liu@brighthealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: ellen.price@brighthealth.com, procurement@brighthealth.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 14:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data Processing Addendum — KMS requirement & signature timeline

Vanessa / Rishi —

Procurement is firm: BYOK (or equivalent HSM control) for the specified dataset is mandatory. They will not proceed to DocuSign unless the DPA includes a clear KMS-related clause and technical approach. We cannot accept a post-signature assessment as a condition — procurement needs comfort that the controls will be in place as contracted.

If Redwood can’t provide BYOK in the hosted product, procurement will consider:
- Limited-scope contract that explicitly restricts processing of identified PHI-derived data to a Dedicated EU deployment, or
- A carve-out that limits Redwood’s processing rights for that dataset until a validated KMS solution is in place.

We need to know which option Redwood prefers by end of day 2026-12-03 to keep the timeline.

Thomas Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
BrightHealth

[Attachment: none]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Data Processing Addendum — KMS requirement & signature timeline

Team — forwarding the latest from BrightHealth. Procurement has drawn a hard line and will not sign without KMS language or an EU residency carve-out. This is now blocking the deal; the revenue impact is material and they want signature this week.

Ask: can we get a risk exception approved for one of these two paths by COB Monday (12/06)?

Suggested options:
- Short path: Offer a Dedicated EU deployment limited to the PHI-derived dataset and include it in the SOW. Procurement signs and we begin onboarding. This requires Ops confirmation of capacity and timeline.
- Engineering path: Commit to an engineering effort to enable BYOK in the hosted product with an estimated go-live (TBD) — but that likely misses procurement's deadline.

Please prioritize the exception ticket (I started a draft here: https://internal.redwood.com/infra/exception-requests/EXC-889). If Legal + Security approve a limited exception (Dedicated EU or scoped processing clause), I’ll propose that to BrightHealth immediately and push for DocuSign execution.

Thanks — Vanessa

[Inline: excerpt of Thomas' note]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, security-leads@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 16:44:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Data Processing Addendum — KMS requirement & signature timeline

Vanessa / Team —

I escalated to Security and Infra. Short answer: Legal cannot approve BYOK in hosted without an architecture review, proof of encryption key lifecycle controls, and threat modeling. That review will take time (estimated 2-3 weeks) and requires infra resources.

Recommended immediate compromise:
1) Offer a Dedicated EU deployment for the PHI-derived dataset under the standard DPA with a narrow SOW that limits processing to specified job flows. This can likely be stood up faster and satisfies data residency concerns. Ops must confirm capacity and timing; Karthik, can you get an ops ETA today?
2) Prepare a conditional clause for the DPA: Redwood will pursue BYOK engineering work with timelines and regular check-ins; any production use of BYOK will be subject to a follow-on amendment after completion of the program and an agreed security attestation. This gives procurement contractual visibility without blocking signature on the residency-based option.

I'll draft the exception packet and the conditional clause language; we should be ready to present to BrightHealth Monday morning. If anyone believes we must commit to BYOK now, escalate to execs — Legal + Security will not sign off without the review.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: Exception_Request_Template.pdf (pdf); Redwood_DPA_standard_v3_redlined.pdf (pdf)]
